# Review: U-2 Control Narrative, Sections 5.1 and 5.2

Two findings are safety-critical and need action before any other edits: F-01 (automatic restart after ESD) and F-02 (blowdown valve fail position).

## Findings

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-01 | 5.2 bullet 3 | **Critical.** The unit restarts automatically when the ESD condition clears. A gas release or fire may have damaged equipment, and no one has checked the area. The cause may still be present, such as a gas leak below the detector setpoint. Operators may be working on the unit. | Latch the ESD. Allow reset only by the operator at the local panel after a field check. Require a new operator Start. Remove all auto-restart. Add FR-U2-020 (below). |
| F-02 | 5.2 bullet 2 | Blowdown valves "fail-closed" on loss of air, power or signal. Station gas then stays trapped when ESD fails. Blowdown valves normally fail open, and the block valves fail closed. The text gives no design basis for this choice. | Confirm the design basis. Unless a documented hazard study says otherwise, specify blowdown valves as fail-open. Add a fail-position table for all U-2 and station valves (see Abnormal handling). Test it at FAT by removing the signal and the air. |
| F-03 | 5.2 bullet 1 and 4 | "Trip value see vendor data" defers a value the document must contain. The text does not say what trips, what stops, whether the trip latches, how it resets, or where valves go. | Put the values in the setpoint list (below). Specify the trip action, the latch, the reset and the bad-PV behavior (FR-U2-014 to 019). |
| F-04 | 5.2 bullet 1 | "Will trip" is not testable. It gives no trip action. | State the action: close the fuel valve, open the recycle valve, remove the start permissive, start the cooldown/lube sequence. |
| F-05 | 5.2 bullet 2 | The station ESD is in the same PLC as the unit control. The narrative describes ESD logic that belongs in the SRS. The text does not say if the ESD is a safety instrumented function or what SIL it has. | Reference the IEC 61511 SRS by document number. Keep only the BPCS-side interface here: ESD input, unit response, and reset. Confirm in the SRS that the ESD is independent of the BPCS functions. Add the open item. |
| F-06 | 5.1 all steps | There are no permissives, no timeouts and no failure responses. A step with no timeout can hang the sequence. | Use the step table below. |
| F-07 | 5.1 Step 2 | "Equals" cannot be tested. The loading valve and the pressure transmitters have no tags. | Use "within the differential in the setpoint list." Add tags: the loading valve, case-pressure and suction-pressure transmitters (tags TBD, open item). |
| F-08 | 5.1 Step 3 | The step has no purge crank before fuel admission. It also omits the light-off timeout, failed ignition, flame loss, hung start and over-temperature. Admitting fuel with no purge risks an explosion in the exhaust. | Add a purge step before fuel. Add failure responses (step table). |
| F-09 | 5.1 Step 4 | The recycle valve closes at idle with no permissive. The text mixes acceleration, recycle closure and loading in one step. It does not describe the surge-control interaction. | Split the step. Close the recycle valve only after the stated condition is met, under the anti-surge controller. Add loading to operating speed as a separate step. |
| F-10 | Whole excerpt | There is no ISA-106 state table. Missing states: Stopped, Starting, Running, Stopping, Tripped, ESD, Held. The text gives no automation levels. | Build the state table first (below). Derive the sequences from it. |
| F-11 | Whole excerpt | There is no normal stop sequence. There is no rule for the compressor case after a stop or trip (hold pressure or vent). The text does not cover an ESD during a start. | Add a stop sequence and the ESD-during-start response. |
| F-12 | Whole excerpt | The excerpt omits bad PV, comms loss and power-loss restart. | Add the abnormal handling table below. |
| F-13 | Whole excerpt | There are no requirement IDs and no test methods. | Use the IDs below. |
| F-14 | Whole excerpt | "Will trip", "is processed by" and "restores throughput" are passive or future wording. "Restores throughput" is a goal, not a requirement. | Rewrite in imperative present tense (STE). |

## Proposed state table (SBC, unit U-2)

| State | Entry permissive | Allowed exits | Initiator | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stopped | Unit stopped and no trip latched | Starting | Operator | Operator-prompted |
| Starting | Start permissives healthy | Running, Held, Tripped, ESD | Auto | Automatic |
| Held | Step condition not met within timeout | Starting (resume), Stopping | Operator | Manual |
| Running | Idle speed reached and recycle valve closed | Stopping, Tripped, ESD | Auto/Operator | Automatic |
| Stopping | Operator Stop | Stopped, Tripped, ESD | Operator | Automatic |
| Tripped | Any unit trip | Stopped | Operator reset | Manual |
| ESD | Station ESD input | Stopped | Operator reset at local panel | Manual |

## Start sequence (replaces 5.1)

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Open the loading valve | Case-to-suction differential within SP-U2-001 | SP-U2-002 | Close the loading valve. Go to Held. Alarm. |
| 2 | Crank to purge (starter) | Purge time SP-U2-003 elapsed at purge speed | SP-U2-004 | Stop the starter. Go to Held. |
| 3 | Admit fuel and energize ignition | Flame detected | SP-U2-005 | Close the fuel valve. Go to Tripped (failed ignition). Require a new purge before any retry. |
| 4 | Accelerate. Disengage the starter at self-sustaining speed. | Idle speed reached | SP-U2-006 | Close the fuel valve. Go to Tripped (hung start). |
| 5 | Close the recycle valve under the anti-surge controller | Recycle valve closed, no surge alarm | SP-U2-007 | Keep the recycle valve open. Go to Held. |
| 6 | Load to operating speed | Operating speed reached | SP-U2-008 | Go to Held. Alarm. |

Flame loss in any running state closes the fuel valve and goes to Tripped.

## Shutdown requirements (replaces 5.2)

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-U2-014 | Trip the unit when the vibration on VT-2201 or VT-2202 is above SP-U2-010 for SP-U2-011. | Inject a signal at FAT. |
| FR-U2-015 | On a unit trip, close the fuel valve and open the recycle valve. | FAT |
| FR-U2-016 | Latch every unit trip. Reset only by the operator after the cause clears. | FAT |
| FR-U2-017 | Alarm a VT-2201/2202 bad-quality signal. Trip if both are bad. Alarm only if one is bad. Use the remaining transmitter. | Fault injection |
| FR-U2-018 | Do not allow Start while a trip is latched. | FAT |
| FR-U2-019 | On station ESD, close the fuel valve before the block valves close. The SRS defines the valve actions. | FAT, per SRS |
| FR-U2-020 | Latch ESD. Do not restart the unit automatically after any ESD, at any time. | FAT: clear the ESD input and confirm there is no start. |
| FR-U2-021 | Allow ESD reset only from the local panel after the ESD input clears. | FAT |

## Abnormal handling

| Event | Unit response |
|---|---|
| Bad PV, case or suction pressure | Hold the start. Alarm. |
| Bad PV, flame detector | Treat as flame loss. Trip. |
| PLC to HMI comms loss | The unit keeps its state. Starts are not possible until comms return. |
| Power loss and restart | The unit goes to Stopped with all trips and ESD latched. Do not resume any sequence. |
| Loss of air or signal | Per the fail-position table below. |

| Valve | Fail position | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Suction and discharge block valves | Closed | Confirm |
| Blowdown valves | **Open** (replaces fail-closed) | Confirm, F-02 |
| Fuel valve | Closed | Confirm |
| Recycle valve | Open | Confirm |
| Loading valve | Closed | Confirm |
